answer:
Target:   minimistjs/minimist @ ecfdaea · checked 2026-11-22
Decision: 🔴 Do not adopt
Confidence: high — All three vulnerability sources answered for both versions; the only gap is that licence and maintenance were read from the repository for 1.2.8, not 1.2.5.

No, do not keep minimist 1.2.5: it has a critical known vulnerability. Upgrade to 1.2.8, which has
no known flaws, is MIT-licensed, and comes from a repository that is still active.

Follow-up
 • Can untrusted people control the arguments or options passed to the parser (for example in a
   server or CI pipeline)? That would make the flaw more urgent.

Why
 🔴 Security: 1.2.5 has a critical known flaw; 1.2.6 and later fix it. (CRA Art. 13(5))
   • minimist 1.2.5 has a critical prototype pollution flaw (CVE-2021-44906), which lets crafted
     input change the behaviour of all objects in the program. It is fixed in 1.2.6.
     "Prototype Pollution in minimist" → https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h ✔
   • The latest version, 1.2.8, has no known vulnerabilities in the sources that answered (OSV,
     GitHub and NVD all responded).
     ""1.2.8": {"malware": [], "vulnerabilities": []}" → https://github.com/minimistjs/minimist ✔
 🟢 Licence: MIT licence: permissive, keep the copyright notice.
   • The licence is MIT, so you may use it commercially. You must keep the copyright and licence
     notice.
     "MIT License Copyright (c) 2013 James Halliday and contributors" → https://github.com/minimistjs/minimist/blob/ecfdaea23e7931c0d529c52b743c711c3278a8ce/LICENSE ✔
 🟢 Maintenance: Repository not archived; commits as recent as December 2025.
   • The project is still active: not archived, and its last commit was in late December 2025. The
     newest npm release, 1.2.8, dates from February 2023.
     ""archived": false, "default_branch": "main", "head_commit": "ecfdaea23e7931c0d529c52b743c711c3278a8ce",…" → https://github.com/minimistjs/minimist ✔

What to do next
 1. Upgrade minimist from 1.2.5 to 1.2.8 (the first fixed version is 1.2.6) and re-run your CLI
   tests.
     Source: "Prototype Pollution in minimist"
     → https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h
 2. Check your lockfile for other copies of minimist pulled in by other packages, and update those
   too.
     Source: "Prototype Pollution in minimist"
     → https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h
 3. After upgrading, confirm the installed version is 1.2.8 and re-run a vulnerability check.
     Source: ""1.2.8": {"malware": [], "vulnerabilities": []}"

report.question: Our Node.js CLI uses minimist@1.2.5 to parse arguments. Can we keep using this version?
assumptions: Licence and maintenance were read from minimistjs/minimist, the repository the registry lists for 1.2.8. The lookup for 1.2.5 pointed to substack/minimist, which no longer exists at that address.
The CLI is internal or run by trusted users; no personal data handling was stated, so privacy was not assessed.

licence.summary: MIT licence: permissive, keep the copyright notice.

security.summary: 1.2.5 has a critical known flaw; 1.2.6 and later fix it.

maintenance.summary: Repository not archived; commits as recent as December 2025.

privacy.summary: Not assessed: no personal data handling was stated for this parser.

findings.claim: minimist 1.2.5 has a critical prototype pollution flaw (CVE-2021-44906), which lets crafted input change the behaviour of all objects in the program. It is fixed in 1.2.6.
findings.why: A critical flaw that affects the exact version in use is a serious problem unless the input is fully trusted.
findings.uncertainty: Real risk depends on whether untrusted people can control the arguments passed to the parser.

findings.claim: The latest version, 1.2.8, has no known vulnerabilities in the sources that answered (OSV, GitHub and NVD all responded).
findings.why: Upgrading to 1.2.8 removes the known flaw.
findings.uncertainty: No advisory does not prove the absence of unknown flaws.

findings.claim: The project is still active: not archived, and its last commit was in late December 2025. The newest npm release, 1.2.8, dates from February 2023.
findings.why: Fixes can still be published if new problems are found.
findings.uncertainty: No release in almost 3 years; the library is small and stable, so this may simply mean it is finished.

findings.claim: The licence is MIT, so you may use it commercially. You must keep the copyright and licence notice.
findings.evidence_quote:
MIT License

Copyright (c) 2013 James Halliday and contributors
findings.why: There is no obligation to release your own source code.
findings.uncertainty: The licence file was read at the latest commit, not at the 1.2.5 tag; the npm record for 1.2.8 also says MIT.

Check your lockfile for other copies of minimist pulled in by other packages, and update those too.
After upgrading, confirm the installed version is 1.2.8 and re-run a vulnerability check.
